notes: First product verdict (loop 1). Read vision.md, PRD, README, the landing, connect and report texts and screenshots, and all 12 judge files. The Berlin beta (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:126-159: German, /try, invite codes, VAT and minimum-wage facts) is mid-edit and earns nothing yet (rule 5), though /try answers Selin's main blocker. Strong: it teaches the method, not just the answer. It has four source labels with a legend (report.txt:85-101), maths in the owner's numbers, a slider whose 'Why this changed' explains (report.txt:489), an 'It can / It cannot' box (report.txt:502-514), a till-side test card with keep/tweak/stop agreed up front (report.txt:811-858) and 'Use this method again' (report.txt:878-894). No 'will'. Personas: Selin 7.0, hackathon 7.4, educator 7.5. Held back: (1) The AI half of 'AI education' is weakest: the demo says both 'played by an AI' and 'with no AI' (report.txt:516, 524), and 'What you learned' has no AI lesson (report.txt:868-873). (2) No owner can use her own numbers without Developer mode or an MCP URL, and there is no live URL (landing.txt:154, 174; README.md:26). (3) The feedback loop, the clearest edge over a chatbot, is never shown. (4) Ceilings that depend on a guess read as facts (report.txt:405, 858).
improvements: Report steps 1 and 5, 'What you learned' and the glossary (report.txt:516 vs 524; src/sim/rehearsal.ts:53 and src/report/rehearsal.ts:20; report.txt:868-873 and 896-906). Make the AI lesson as explicit as the decision lesson. Derive the caveat from the rehearsal method, so the report makes one claim about who played the customers. Add a three-line 'Who did what' card to step 1, built from the share state: from you (13 numbers); calculated by plain code (the figures); guesses (4, which only the test can check); done by an AI (asked the questions and played the customers, or nothing on a rule-based or /try run). Add one AI lesson to 'What you learned' ('Next time any AI gives you a number, ask: is it yours, calculated, a guess or imagined?') and an 'AI model' entry to the glossary. Why: fit with AI education (25%). The hackathon judge named it the weakest part, and all three personas flagged the contradiction. It worked when Selin can answer 'what did the AI do in this report?' from the page, and report.txt holds no contradiction.

Own numbers and a live link (landing.txt:154, 174; connect-phone.png; README.md:26-29; report.txt:7). Ship the planned /try wizard (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:157-159) and deploy. Then point the demo ribbon 'Swap in your own to get your answer' at /try, put the live demo link and /try at the top of the README, and move ChatGPT Developer mode, Cursor and VS Code behind 'For developers'. Why: feasible on Monday (15%), and a judge gets it in 60 seconds (10%). Selin stopped at 'Developer mode', and the other judges found only YOUR-SITE or a dead what-if-coach.vercel.app. It worked when a judge reaches the demo from the README in one click, and Selin reaches a report with her own 140 customers and €7.40 from her phone, in German, without an AI app.

The feedback loop. Landing step 7 promises it (landing.txt:96-102), and resultBlock exists (src/report/sections.ts:401), but no demo shows it. Publish a clearly labelled sample 'after the test' report: for example, 6 extra a day counted and 40% of deal buyers already lunch regulars. Show 'Where reality landed' beside cautious, expected and optimistic, plus what to change next time. Link it from landing step 7 and from the report's 'When the test is done, come back'. Why: more useful than a chatbot (15%) and vision core step 6; the hackathon judge and the educator both asked for it. It worked when a judge sees the guesses next to reality in the demo within two clicks.

Certainty and countability in the money lines. 'That is the most it can cost' (report.txt:405) and 'cannot cost more than €560' (report.txt:858) rest on the 30% switching guess. The headline −€56.02 (report.txt:61, 489) does not match 12.40 × 10 − 180 = −56.00. The €370 stop line includes regulars' discounts that are not in the receipts envelope (report.txt:839, 858). Name the guess each ceiling rests on: 'if 30% of your lunch regulars switch, as you guessed; if half switch, about €660'. Show test results in whole euros, and make every stop-line number one Selin can count from the tally sheet, the Z-report or the envelope. Why: honesty (15%). These sentences sit one step from the certainty cap, and Selin could not tell when she had 'spent €370'. It worked when no owner-facing string states a ceiling without its guess, and every 'Why this changed' sum checks out on a phone calculator.

Scope honesty for questions What-IF cannot model. The README's 'Just say what if…' section says such questions are mapped 'openly', yet qa/judge/mcp.json and skill.json found 'hire a part-timer', 'what if it rains tomorrow' and 'put my cakes down to €3' all sent to the lunch-deal questions. For hiring and opening hours, return 'What-IF cannot model this yet', plus the paper method from 'Use this method again' (report.txt:878-894). Recognise price cuts as price changes, and reframe questions that are not decisions. Why: honesty, and 'What-IF is not a fortune teller'. Owners in the Berlin beta will bring their real questions on day one. It worked when the README's six examples each reach the right template or an honest 'not yet'.

Demo coherence. The landing says 'Seven small steps' (landing.txt:37), the report 'Step 6/6' (report.txt:15). The landing teaser shows 'Mia told Jonas' and '3 of 6 tried it' (landing.txt:129, 140), but the demo shows 0 of 6 (report.txt:533-540). The QA screenshots use seed 42, while /r#demo uses seed 23 (qa/checks.ts:257 vs src/report/demo.ts:22). Quote only what the shipped demo shows, count the steps the same way on both pages, and add one sentence to step 5 that sets the rehearsal count beside the likely guess of 8 without merging the two. Why: a teaser that shows results the demo does not have is a small honesty slip. Selin and the educator also worried that '0 of 6' reads as 'the AI says nobody will come'. It worked when every quote and count on the landing page appears in /r#demo.
